66834.q: What is the life energy that flows through everything called in Daoism?
66834.e: In Chinese thought, qi (also written chi) is the life force that flows in people and nature. Exercises such as qigong are meant to strengthen it.
66834.m: In Chinese thought, qi is the life energy.

66835.q: Which slow movement art is closely linked to Daoist thought?
66835.e: Taijiquan (tai chi) is made up of flowing, slow movements. It is based on the idea of yin and yang and the harmonious flow of qi.
66835.m: Taijiquan combines slow movement with Daoist thought.

66836.q: In a famous story, what did the Daoist thinker Zhuangzi dream?
a: That he could fly like a dragon
66836.e: Zhuangzi woke up and wondered whether he was a man who had dreamt of being a butterfly, or a butterfly dreaming of being a man.
66836.m: Zhuangzi dreamt he was a butterfly.

66837.q: According to Daoist teaching, how should a person live?
a: As rich and powerful as possible
66837.e: Daoism teaches that you should follow the natural order and live simply. Whoever goes against the flow of things loses their strength.
66837.m: Daoists want to live in harmony with nature and the Dao.

66838.q: Which black and white sign stands for the balance of opposites in Daoism?
66838.e: Yin and yang show two opposites, such as light and dark, that belong together and complete each other.
66838.m: Yin and yang stand for opposites that belong together.

66839.q: What stands on the home altar for the ancestors in many Chinese families?
66839.e: On the home altar there are wooden tablets with the names of the dead. People put food in front of them and light incense sticks.
66839.m: Ancestor tablets on the home altar remind people of the dead.

66840.q: What do many Chinese people light for their ancestors?
66840.e: The smoke of incense sticks is meant to create a link to the ancestors. People often bow in front of the altar as they do this.
66840.m: In China, incense sticks are part of honouring the ancestors.

66841.q: What do families in China often burn as a gift for the dead?
66841.e: People burn so-called spirit money and paper houses, paper cars or paper clothes. According to the belief, the ancestors receive these things in the afterlife.
66841.m: Burned paper money is meant to serve the ancestors in the afterlife.

66842.q: What buildings did large Chinese family groups build for their shared ancestors?
66842.e: A family group (clan) often had its own ancestral hall. The ancestor tablets stood there, and people met there for ceremonies.
66842.m: Chinese family groups honoured their ancestors in ancestral halls.

66843.q: What is the festival on the 15th day of the seventh lunar month, when wandering spirits are fed, called?
66843.e: According to folk belief, the gates of the afterlife are open in the seventh lunar month. At the Ghost Festival, people put out food for hungry spirits whom nobody honours any more.
66843.m: At the Chinese Ghost Festival, wandering spirits are fed.

66844.q: Why is honouring ancestors so important in Confucianism?
a: It shows respect for parents even after death
It brings money for the state
66844.e: According to Confucian teaching, respect for your parents does not end with death. Through offerings and remembrance, the family stays connected over generations.
66844.m: Honouring ancestors continues respect for parents beyond death.

66845.q: In a traditional Chinese family, who usually led the ceremonies for the ancestors?
66845.e: Traditionally, the eldest son was responsible for the offerings to the ancestors. That is why it used to be very important to have a son.
66845.m: Traditionally, the eldest son led the ancestor ceremonies.

66846.q: Which colour is traditionally the colour of mourning in China?
66846.e: At traditional Chinese funerals, the family wear white mourning clothes. Red, on the other hand, is the colour of happiness and is worn at weddings.
66846.m: In China, white is traditionally the colour of mourning.

66847.q: What is the Qingming Festival often called in English?
66847.e: The name Tomb-Sweeping Day already shows what it is about: the festival is dedicated to the ancestors who have died. It is one of the most important days of remembrance in China.
66847.m: At the Qingming Festival, families look after their ancestors’ graves.

66848.q: When does the Qingming Festival usually take place?
66848.e: The Qingming Festival follows the solar year and usually falls on 4 or 5 April, rarely on 6 April. It is one of the few Chinese festivals with an almost fixed date.
66848.m: The Qingming Festival usually falls on 4 or 5 April.

66849.q: What does the name “Qingming” roughly mean?
66849.e: Qingming means “clear and bright” and describes the spring weather. It is also the name of one of the 24 sections of the Chinese solar year.

66850.q: What do families do at their ancestors’ graves at the Qingming Festival?
a: They clean the grave and bring gifts
66850.e: People pull out weeds, sweep the grave and bring food, flowers and incense sticks. In this way they show respect to the dead.
66850.m: At the Qingming Festival, graves are cleaned and decorated.

66851.q: Which outdoor pastime is traditionally also part of the Qingming Festival?
66851.e: Because the festival is in spring, many families also go on outings. Traditionally they fly kites.
66851.m: Spring outings and kite flying are also part of the Qingming Festival.

66852.q: What do many people in China do at the Qingming Festival because it is a public holiday?
a: They travel to their home towns
They go on a skiing holiday
They stay in bed all day
66852.e: Since 2008 the Qingming Festival has again been a public holiday in the People’s Republic of China. Many people then travel to their home towns to visit their ancestors’ graves.
66852.m: At the Qingming Festival, many people travel to their home towns.

66853.q: Which older festival, when people only ate cold food, is closely linked to Qingming?
66853.e: At the Hanshi Festival, traditionally no fire could be lit, so people ate cold food. It was shortly before Qingming and later merged with it.
66853.m: The Cold Food Festival became part of the Qingming Festival.

66854.q: Apart from China, where else is the Qingming Festival celebrated?
66854.e: Qingming is also an important day in Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau and for many Chinese people abroad. In Taiwan and Hong Kong it is a public holiday.
66854.m: The Qingming Festival is celebrated wherever many Chinese people live.

66855.q: When does the Chinese Dragon Boat Festival usually fall in our calendar?
a: At the end of May or in June
66855.e: The Dragon Boat Festival falls on the 5th day of the 5th lunar month. In the Western calendar it is at the end of May or in June.
66855.m: The Dragon Boat Festival is at the end of May or in June.

66856.q: Who was Qu Yuan, whom the Dragon Boat Festival remembers?
a: A poet who drowned in a river
A fisherman who invented a boat
A warrior who built a wall
66856.e: Qu Yuan was a Chinese poet and minister. In despair over the fall of his country, he drowned himself in the Miluo River.
66856.m: The Dragon Boat Festival remembers the poet Qu Yuan.

66857.q: Which food is traditionally eaten at the Dragon Boat Festival?
66857.e: Zongzi are parcels of sticky rice wrapped in bamboo or reed leaves and cooked. They are often filled with meat, beans or dates.
66857.m: Zongzi made of sticky rice are part of the Dragon Boat Festival.

66858.q: According to legend, why did people throw rice into the river after Qu Yuan had drowned?
a: So the fish would leave his body alone
So the river would be clean
So the boats would go faster
66858.e: The fishermen wanted to feed the fish with rice so that they would not eat the poet’s body. Zongzi are said to have come from this later.
66858.m: According to legend, rice in the river was meant to protect Qu Yuan’s body.

66859.q: In a dragon boat race, what sets the rhythm for the paddlers?
66859.e: At the front of the boat sits a person with a large drum. The beat helps the team paddle at the same time.
66859.m: In a dragon boat race, a drum sets the rhythm.

66860.q: What do the boats in a dragon boat race represent?
a: Dragons with a head and tail
66860.e: Dragon boats are long, narrow boats with a carved dragon’s head at the front and a dragon’s tail at the back. In China the dragon is seen as the ruler of water.
66860.m: Dragon boats have a dragon’s head at the front and a tail at the back.

66861.q: In which country did the Dragon Boat Festival begin?
66861.e: The Dragon Boat Festival comes from China. Today there are dragon boat races all over the world, including in Switzerland.
66861.m: The Dragon Boat Festival comes from China.

66862.q: Which plant do many families hang on the door at the Dragon Boat Festival to keep bad luck away?
66862.e: According to old belief, mugwort and sweet flag ward off illness and evil spirits. The fifth month used to be seen as a dangerous time.
66862.m: Mugwort on the door is meant to keep bad luck away at the Dragon Boat Festival.

66863.q: According to Shinto belief, where can kami live?
66863.e: In Shinto, kami are divine beings and forces. They can live in things in nature such as mountains, waterfalls, trees or rocks.
66863.m: In Shinto, kami can live in nature.

66864.q: According to a Japanese saying, how many kami are there?
66864.e: People speak of “yaoyorozu no kami”, the eight million kami. The number simply means “countless”.
66864.m: In Shinto, people speak of eight million, meaning countless, kami.

66865.q: In Shinto, what are holy trees or rocks where kami live marked with?
66865.e: A braided rope made of rice straw is called a shimenawa. White paper strips in a zigzag shape often hang from it.
66865.m: A shimenawa rope shows that a place is holy in Shinto.

66866.q: What is the popular kami Inari responsible for?
66866.e: Inari is the kami of rice, of fertile fields and of prosperity. Thousands of shrines in Japan are dedicated to Inari.
66866.m: In Shinto, Inari is the kami of rice and prosperity.

66867.q: Which animals are seen as messengers of the kami Inari?
66867.e: Stone fox figures often stand in front of Inari shrines. They are seen as messengers of the kami.
66867.m: Foxes are the messengers of the kami Inari.

66868.q: What are the priests at a Shinto shrine called?
66868.e: Kannushi look after the shrine and carry out ceremonies for the kami. They are often helped by young women in white and red, the miko.

66869.q: At Shinto shrines, what do visitors write their wishes to the kami on?
66869.e: These little wooden tablets are called ema and often have a picture painted on them. People hang them up at the shrine so the kami can read the wishes.
66869.m: Wishes to the kami are written on wooden ema tablets.

66870.q: How do many people in Japan combine Shinto and Buddhism?
a: They often follow both at the same time
66870.e: In Japan it is usual to keep Shinto festivals and Buddhist rituals side by side. People often say: birth in Shinto, funeral in Buddhism.
66870.m: Many people in Japan practise Shinto and Buddhism side by side.

66871.q: Which goddess is Amaterasu in Shinto?
66871.e: Amaterasu is the goddess of the sun and is seen as the most important deity of Shinto. Her name means something like “the one who shines in heaven”.
66871.m: Amaterasu is the sun goddess of Shinto.

66872.q: In the myth, where did Amaterasu withdraw to, so that the world became dark?
66872.e: Amaterasu was so angry with her wild brother that she hid in the heavenly rock cave. Without her, it became dark everywhere in the world.
66872.m: When Amaterasu hid in a cave, the world became dark.

66873.q: In the myth, who was Amaterasu so angry with that she hid in a cave?
66873.e: Her brother Susanoo, the god of storms, caused great damage. That is why the sun goddess withdrew.
66873.m: Amaterasu hid because of her stormy brother.

66874.q: How did the gods lure Amaterasu out of her cave?
a: With dancing, laughter and a mirror
66874.e: The goddess Ame-no-Uzume danced so funnily that all the gods laughed. Curious, Amaterasu looked out, saw her reflection in a mirror and was pulled out.
66874.m: A dance, laughter and a mirror brought Amaterasu out of the cave.

66875.q: According to Japanese tradition, who is descended from Amaterasu?
66875.e: According to the myth, the first emperor, Jimmu, was a descendant of the sun goddess. This used to be the reason given for the emperor’s special position.
66875.m: According to the myth, the Japanese imperial family goes back to Amaterasu.

66876.q: In which country is the sun goddess Amaterasu worshipped?
66876.e: Amaterasu is the most important deity of Shinto, the old religion of Japan. The red sun on Japan’s flag is a reminder of the “Land of the Rising Sun”.
66876.m: Amaterasu is a goddess from Japan.

66877.q: Which three objects make up the Japanese imperial regalia?
66877.e: According to the myth, the three imperial treasures come from Amaterasu. They are used when an emperor comes to the throne but are never shown in public.
66877.m: Mirror, sword and jewel are the regalia of the Japanese emperor.

66878.q: In which country is the Ise Shrine?
66878.e: The Ise Shrine (Ise Jingu) is in the city of Ise in Mie Prefecture. It is seen as the most important shrine of Shinto.
66878.m: The Ise Shrine is the most important Shinto shrine in Japan.

66879.q: To which goddess is the Inner Shrine of Ise dedicated?
66879.e: The Inner Shrine is dedicated to the sun goddess Amaterasu. The Outer Shrine honours the goddess of food.
66879.m: The Inner Shrine of Ise is dedicated to the sun goddess.

66880.q: Every how many years are the main buildings of the Ise Shrine rebuilt?
66880.e: For over 1300 years, the main buildings have been rebuilt every 20 years next to the old site. This keeps the knowledge of the old craftsmanship alive.
66880.m: The Ise Shrine is rebuilt every 20 years.

66881.q: Why are the buildings of the Ise Shrine rebuilt again and again?
a: So the old craft is passed on
Because people want to change the colour
66881.e: The main buildings are rebuilt every 20 years, most recently in 2013. In this way young craftspeople learn the old building skills from older ones.
66881.m: Rebuilding keeps the old craft alive.

66882.q: What do the buildings of the Ise Shrine look like?
66882.e: They are built with the light wood of the Japanese cypress (hinoki). The buildings are put up in the old style and are not painted.
66882.m: The Ise Shrine is built of light, unpainted wood.

66883.q: Which sacred object is said to be kept in the Inner Shrine of Ise?
66883.e: The sacred mirror Yata no Kagami is seen as the seat of the sun goddess. It is said to be kept in Ise, but nobody is allowed to look at it.
66883.m: The sacred mirror is kept in the Inner Shrine of Ise.

66884.q: What does the Ise Shrine complex consist of?
66884.e: Besides the Inner and Outer Shrines, the Ise Shrine includes many smaller shrines, about 125 in total.
66884.m: The Ise Shrine is a complex made up of many shrines.

66885.q: What is another name for a Japanese rock garden without water?
66885.e: In Japanese it is called karesansui, literally “dry mountain and water landscape”. Water is shown there only with gravel or sand.
66885.m: A Zen garden is a dry landscape garden.

66886.q: What does the raked gravel in a Zen garden usually represent?
66886.e: The lines in the gravel look like waves on a lake or sea. Stones in it look like islands or mountains.
66886.m: In a Zen garden, raked gravel represents water and waves.

66887.q: Who rakes the patterns into the gravel of temple Zen gardens?
66887.e: In Zen temples, monks rake the patterns again regularly. This calm work is itself seen as a form of meditation.
66887.m: Monks rake the patterns into the gravel of Zen gardens.

66888.q: Which temple in Kyoto has the most famous Zen rock garden?
66888.e: The rock garden of Ryoan-ji is made of white gravel and a few groups of stones. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage in Kyoto.
66888.m: Ryoan-ji in Kyoto has the most famous Zen rock garden.

66889.q: What is special about the rock garden of Ryoan-ji?
a: You can never see all the stones at once
The stones are made of gold
66889.e: There are 15 stones in five groups in the garden. But from any spot on the veranda you can see at most 14 of them.
66889.m: At Ryoan-ji you never see all the stones at the same time.

66890.q: What is a Zen garden mainly for?
66890.e: You usually do not walk into a Zen garden but look at it quietly from a veranda. It is meant to help you become calm and focused.
66890.m: A Zen garden invites quiet contemplation and meditation.

66891.q: From which country did Zen Buddhism come to Japan?
66891.e: Zen Buddhism began in China, where it is called Chan. Japanese monks brought it to Japan in the 12th and 13th centuries.
66891.m: Zen Buddhism came to Japan from China.

66892.q: Which plant grows as a soft green carpet in many Japanese temple gardens?
66892.e: Many kinds of moss grow in the damp gardens of Kyoto, for example at the famous Moss Temple, Saiho-ji. Moss stands for age and calm.
66892.m: Moss is part of many Japanese temple gardens.

66893.q: Who do people in Japan honour at the Obon festival?
66893.e: According to the belief, the souls of the dead return to their families for a few days at the Obon festival. They are welcomed and sent off again with rituals.
66893.m: At the Obon festival in Japan, people honour the souls of their ancestors.

66894.q: In which month is Obon celebrated in most regions of Japan?
66894.e: Obon is usually celebrated from 13 to 16 August. In some areas, such as Tokyo, it takes place in July.
66894.m: Obon is usually celebrated in mid-August.

66895.q: Which religion does the Obon festival originally come from?
66895.e: Obon goes back to a Buddhist story: a student of Buddha wanted to help his dead mother. Today the festival combines Buddhist customs with old ancestor worship.
66895.m: The Obon festival has Buddhist roots.

66896.q: How do people usually dance at Bon Odori during the Obon festival?
a: In a circle around a stand with drummers
On ice skates on a lake
66896.e: At Bon Odori, many people dance in a circle around a stand with drummers. The dances welcome the souls of the ancestors.
66896.m: At Bon Odori, people dance in a circle.

66897.q: What do people in some places float on rivers at the end of Obon?
66897.e: At Toro Nagashi, glowing paper lanterns are placed on the water. They are meant to guide the souls back to the afterlife.
66897.m: Floating lanterns guide the souls back at the end of Obon.

66898.q: At Obon, which animal is made out of a cucumber so the souls can come home quickly?
66898.e: Sticks turn the cucumber into a horse. An aubergine becomes a cow so that the souls return slowly at the end.
66898.m: At Obon, a cucumber horse is meant to bring the souls quickly.

66899.q: What is lit on the mountainsides in Kyoto at the end of Obon?
a: Huge fires in the shape of written characters
Thousands of candles in the snow
66899.e: At Gozan no Okuribi on 16 August, five huge fires burn on mountains around Kyoto. The best known shows the character for “big”.
66899.m: In Kyoto, huge mountain fires send off the souls at the end of Obon.

66900.q: Why are trains and roads in Japan often very full at Obon?
a: Many people travel to their home towns
The shops close for a year
66900.e: At Obon, many people visit their families and their ancestors’ graves in their home towns. It is one of the busiest travel times in Japan.
66900.m: At Obon, many Japanese people travel to their families.

66901.q: What does the name of the festival Shichi-Go-San mean?
66901.e: Shichi means seven, go means five and san means three. It refers to the ages of the children who are celebrated.

66902.q: On which date is Shichi-Go-San traditionally celebrated?
66902.e: The traditional day is 15 November. Today many families also visit the shrines at the weekends before or after.

66903.q: Which children are especially celebrated at Shichi-Go-San?
66903.e: Traditionally, girls are celebrated at the ages of three and seven, and boys at five. In some regions three-year-old boys are celebrated too.
66903.m: At Shichi-Go-San, girls aged 3 and 7 and boys aged 5 are celebrated.

66904.q: Where do families go with their children at Shichi-Go-San?
66904.e: At the shrine, families give thanks that their children are growing up healthy. They ask the kami for a long and happy life.
66904.m: At Shichi-Go-San, families visit a Shinto shrine.

66905.q: What does the long shape of the sugar sticks that children get at Shichi-Go-San stand for?
66905.e: The sweet is called chitose-ame, “thousand-year sweet”. The long red and white sugar sticks stand for a long life.
66905.m: Chitose-ame wishes children a long life.

66906.q: In Japan, children aged 3, 5 and 7 celebrate a special festival. What do many of them wear for it?
66906.e: The festival is called Shichi-Go-San. Many children wear a festive kimono for the first time.
66906.m: At Shichi-Go-San, many children wear a festive kimono.

66907.q: Why did people in Japan used to celebrate reaching certain ages in childhood so solemnly?
a: Many children used to die very young
Children were then allowed to marry
Children then had to become soldiers
66907.e: In the past, many children died young. So when a child reached a certain age, people gave special thanks that it had survived.
66907.m: Shichi-Go-San came from gratitude that children had survived.

66908.q: What was the Egyptian Book of the Dead for?
a: To help the dead in the afterlife
As the pharaoh’s book of laws
As the recipe book of the temple kitchen
As a calendar for the Nile flood
66908.e: The Book of the Dead was a collection of spells meant to make sure the dead person got safely through the underworld. It was placed in the grave.
66908.m: The Book of the Dead was meant to guide the dead safely through the afterlife.

66909.q: On what material was the Egyptian Book of the Dead usually written?
66909.e: Most Books of the Dead are papyrus scrolls. Papyrus was made from the papyrus plant, which grew along the Nile.
66909.m: The Egyptians wrote their Books of the Dead on papyrus.

66910.q: Where did the Egyptians put the Book of the Dead?
a: In the grave with the dead person
66910.e: The Book of the Dead was placed in the grave, often in the coffin or with the mummy. It was meant to help the dead person leave the grave by day and reach the afterlife.
66910.m: The Book of the Dead was placed in the grave with the dead person.

66911.q: Who was the first to decipher hieroglyphs, so that texts like the Book of the Dead could be read?
66911.e: Champollion deciphered hieroglyphs in 1822 with the help of the Rosetta Stone. Only after that could people understand ancient Egyptian texts such as the Book of the Dead.

66912.q: What did the Egyptian Book of the Dead mainly contain?
66912.e: The Book of the Dead was a collection of spells. They were meant to protect the dead person and open the way through the underworld. Older forerunners were the Pyramid Texts and the Coffin Texts.
66912.m: The Book of the Dead is a collection of spells.

66913.q: Where can you see real Egyptian Books of the Dead today?
66913.e: Many Books of the Dead are on display in museums. One of the most beautiful, the Papyrus of Ani, is in the British Museum in London.
66913.m: Egyptian Books of the Dead can be seen in museums today.

66914.q: What do the coloured pictures in the Egyptian Book of the Dead show, for example?
a: The dead person before the gods
66914.e: The small pictures in the Book of the Dead are called vignettes. They show, for example, how the dead person’s heart is weighed before the gods.
66914.m: Pictures in the Book of the Dead show the dead person before the gods.

66915.q: Which amulet with a spell from the Book of the Dead was placed on the mummy’s chest?
66915.e: The heart scarab usually carried spell 30. It was meant to stop the heart from speaking against the dead person at the judgement.
66915.m: The heart scarab was meant to keep the dead person’s heart silent.

66916.q: In which period of Egyptian history did the Book of the Dead on papyrus become common?
66916.e: The Book of the Dead came into use at the start of the New Kingdom around 1550 BC. It was used until the Late Period.
66916.m: The Book of the Dead became common in the New Kingdom.

66917.q: Which realm did the Egyptian god Osiris rule?
66917.e: Osiris was the ruler of the afterlife. According to the myth, he became king of the dead after his death.
66917.m: Osiris was the king of the realm of the dead.

66918.q: In the myth, which brother murdered the god Osiris?
66918.e: The jealous Seth killed Osiris and cut him into pieces. Seth was seen as the god of chaos and the desert.

66919.q: Which goddess gathered the pieces of her murdered husband Osiris?
66919.e: Isis found the pieces of Osiris and brought him back to life with her magic. She was one of the most important goddesses of Egypt.
66919.m: Isis brought Osiris back with her magic.

66920.q: Which falcon-headed god was the son of Osiris?
66920.e: Horus avenged his father and fought Seth for the throne. Every pharaoh was seen as a living Horus.
66920.m: Horus is the son of Osiris and Isis.

66921.q: In which colour was Osiris’s skin often shown, as a sign of new life?
66921.e: Osiris was often painted with green or black skin. Green stood for plants growing and for rebirth.
66921.m: Osiris’s green skin stands for new life.

66922.q: What was placed on the scales at the Egyptian judgement of the dead?
66922.e: The heart was seen as the seat of reason and conscience. It was weighed against a feather.
66922.m: At the judgement of the dead, the heart of the dead person was weighed.

66923.q: Whose feather lay in the other pan of the scales at the judgement of the dead?
66923.e: Maat was the goddess of truth and order. A good heart could not be heavier than her feather.
66923.m: The heart had to be as light as the feather of Maat.

66924.q: Which jackal-headed god worked the scales at the judgement of the dead?
66924.e: Anubis was the god of embalming and went with the dead. He watched over the weighing of the heart.

66925.q: Which god wrote down the result of the weighing at the judgement of the dead?
66925.e: Thoth was the god of scribes and wisdom and was often shown with the head of an ibis. He recorded the verdict in writing.
66925.m: Thoth was the scribe at the judgement of the dead.

66926.q: According to Egyptian belief, what happened if a dead person’s heart was heavier than the feather?
a: The dead person went to paradise
The heart was covered in gold
66926.e: If someone failed the judgement of the dead, their heart was swallowed by Ammit, “the Devourer”, a creature that was part crocodile, part lion and part hippopotamus.
66926.m: A heavy heart was eaten by a monster.

66927.q: What did a dead person have to do before the judges at the Egyptian judgement of the dead?
a: Declare that they had done no evil deeds
66927.e: Before the gods, the dead person listed the sins they had not committed. According to the Book of the Dead, there were 42 judges.
66927.m: At the judgement of the dead, the dead person declared their innocence.

66928.q: Which god did Pharaoh Akhenaten worship as the only one?
66928.e: Akhenaten placed the sun god Aten above all other gods. This was a big change in Egypt.
66928.m: Akhenaten worshipped mainly the sun god Aten.

66929.q: How was the god Aten usually shown?
a: As a sun disc with rays ending in hands
As a man with a falcon’s head
As a woman with cow horns
As a crocodile in the Nile
66929.e: Aten appeared as a sun disc. Its rays end in small hands, which often hold the ankh, the sign of life.
66929.m: Aten was shown as a sun disc with rays.

66930.q: Why did Pharaoh Akhenaten change his name?
a: In honour of the sun god Aten
Because he had conquered a country
66930.e: Akhenaten came to the throne under a different name. Later he called himself Akhenaten, which means something like “useful to Aten”.
66930.m: Akhenaten named himself after the god Aten.

66931.q: What did Akhenaten have built for the god Aten?
66931.e: Akhenaten founded a new capital called “Horizon of the Aten”. Today the site is called Amarna.
66931.m: Akhenaten built a new capital for Aten.

66932.q: Which famous queen was Akhenaten’s chief wife?
66932.e: Nefertiti was Akhenaten’s great royal wife. Her painted bust is now in the Neues Museum in Berlin.
66932.m: Nefertiti was the wife of Akhenaten.

66933.q: Which famous pharaoh was probably a son of Akhenaten?
66933.e: According to DNA tests, Tutankhamun was very probably Akhenaten’s son. Under him, the old gods were worshipped again.
66933.m: Tutankhamun was probably the son of Akhenaten.

66934.q: Whose cult did Akhenaten fight against, having his name chiselled away?
66934.e: Before that, Amun had been the most powerful god, with rich priests in Thebes. Akhenaten had his name removed from monuments.
66934.m: Akhenaten fought against the worship of the god Amun.

66935.q: What happened to Akhenaten’s new faith after his death?
a: The old gods were worshipped again
All of Egypt kept the Aten faith
The faith spread as far as Rome
It became the faith of all pharaohs
66935.e: After Akhenaten’s death, Egypt returned to the old gods. Tutankhamun also had the old temples reopened.
66935.m: After Akhenaten, the old gods returned.

66936.q: Which text from Akhenaten’s time praises the sun as the creator of all life?
a: The Great Hymn to the Aten
66936.e: The Great Hymn to the Aten was found in the tomb of an official in Amarna. It praises Aten, who keeps people, animals and plants alive.
66936.m: The Great Hymn to the Aten is a song of praise to the sun.

66937.q: What was the name of the priestess who gave the prophecies at Delphi?
66937.e: The Pythia sat on a tripod in the temple and spoke the god’s answers. Priests interpreted her words.
66937.m: The priestess of Delphi was called the Pythia.

66938.q: Which famous saying was written on the temple of Apollo at Delphi?
66938.e: The saying “Gnothi seauton” could be read over the entrance. It reminded people to know their limits.
66938.m: At Delphi the saying “Know thyself” was written.

66939.q: What did the ancient Greeks think Delphi was?
66939.e: According to legend, Zeus let two eagles fly, and they met over Delphi. A stone called the omphalos marked this navel of the world.
66939.m: Delphi was seen as the navel of the world.

66940.q: In which country is ancient Delphi?
66940.e: Delphi lies on the southern slope of Mount Parnassus in central Greece. The oracle was the most famous in the Greek world.

66941.q: Which rich king of Lydia misunderstood a prophecy from Delphi?
66941.e: The oracle said that he would destroy a great empire if he crossed the river Halys. The empire he destroyed was his own.
66941.m: Croesus misread the oracle and lost his empire.

66942.q: Which dragon-like monster is Apollo said to have killed at Delphi?
66942.e: According to the myth, the serpent Python guarded the place. Apollo killed it and founded his sanctuary.
66942.m: At Delphi, Apollo defeated the dragon Python.

66943.q: What were the games held every four years at Delphi called?
66943.e: The Pythian Games honoured Apollo. Besides sport, there were important music competitions there.
66943.m: The Pythian Games were celebrated at Delphi.

66944.q: From which year does the first recorded list of winners of the Olympic Games come?
66944.e: According to tradition, the lists of winners began in 776 BC. After that, the Greeks counted their years in Olympiads.
66944.m: The first recorded Olympic Games took place in 776 BC.

66945.q: What did a winner at the ancient Olympic Games receive as a prize?
66945.e: The wreath was cut from a sacred olive tree in Olympia. Back home, winners often received further honours.
66945.m: Olympic winners received a wreath of olive branches.

66946.q: What was the four-year period between two Games called?
66946.e: An Olympiad is really the period of time between two Games. Today the word is often used for the Games themselves.

66947.q: Which wonder of the ancient world stood in the temple at Olympia?
66947.e: The statue of Zeus, made of gold and ivory, was about 12 metres tall. It was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World and was made by the sculptor Phidias.
66947.m: The statue of Zeus at Olympia was a wonder of the world.

66948.q: Which event is seen as the oldest of the ancient Olympic Games?
66948.e: The stadion race was run over one length of the stadium, at Olympia just under 200 metres. For a long time it was the only event.
66948.m: The stadion race was the oldest Olympic event.

66949.q: What was supposed to apply during the ancient Olympic Games so that everyone could travel safely to Olympia?
66949.e: The ekecheiria was a sacred truce. Athletes and spectators were meant to be able to travel safely to Olympia.
66949.m: During the Games there was a sacred truce.

66950.q: In honour of which goddess were there separate races for girls at Olympia?
66950.e: At the Heraia, unmarried young women raced in three age groups. The winners received a wreath and part of a cow that had been sacrificed.
66950.m: At the Heraia, girls ran in honour of Hera.

66951.q: What did the Lares protect in ancient Rome?
66951.e: The Lares were protective gods of the house. They watched over the family and everyone living in the house.
66951.m: The Lares protected the Romans’ houses.

66952.q: Where did Roman families worship their household gods, the Lares?
a: At a small altar in the house
66952.e: The household altar was called a lararium. It was a niche or small shrine with figures of the household gods.
66952.m: The household altar of the Lares is called a lararium.

66953.q: What did the Roman household gods called the Penates watch over?
66953.e: The Penates protected the store cupboard. The Lares and Penates were often worshipped together.
66953.m: The Penates watched over the household’s food stores.

66954.q: For the Romans, who did the genius of a house protect?
66954.e: The genius was the personal guardian spirit of the head of the family. In the lararium he was often shown as a man with an offering bowl.
66954.m: The genius was the guardian spirit of the father of the household.

66955.q: What did a Roman family offer to its Lares?
66955.e: At meals and festivals the Lares received small gifts. These included food, wine, flowers and incense.
66955.m: The Lares received small gifts such as food and wine.

66956.q: How were the Lares usually shown in pictures?
a: As dancing young men with a drinking horn
As old women with a spinning wheel
66956.e: Typically there are two youths in short tunics. They dance and hold a drinking horn and a bowl.
66956.m: Lares often appear as dancing youths with a drinking horn.

66957.q: Where were the Lares Compitales worshipped?
66957.e: The Lares Compitales protected the crossroads of the neighbourhood. The Compitalia festival was held in their honour.
66957.m: The Lares Compitales watched over crossroads.

66958.q: In which town buried by Vesuvius are many lararia well preserved?
66958.e: The eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79 buried Pompeii under ash. Because of this, many painted household altars were preserved.
66958.m: You can see many lararia in Pompeii.

66959.q: What does the Greek name “Pantheon” mean?
66959.e: “Pan” means all and “theos” means god. The temple was probably dedicated to many gods.
66959.m: Pantheon means “temple of all the gods”.

66960.q: What is at the top in the middle of the Pantheon’s dome?
66960.e: The round opening is called the oculus and is about 9 metres across. Apart from the entrance, it is the only source of light inside.
66960.m: Light falls into the Pantheon through a round opening in the dome.

66961.q: Under which emperor was today’s Pantheon built?
66961.e: Today’s building was put up roughly between AD 118 and 125 under Emperor Hadrian.
66961.m: Emperor Hadrian had today’s Pantheon built.

66962.q: In which language is the inscription above the entrance of the Pantheon written?
66962.e: The Latin inscription names Marcus Agrippa, who had put up a first building. Hadrian had it put back when the new one was built.
66962.m: There is a Latin inscription above the entrance of the Pantheon.

66963.q: Why is the Pantheon in Rome still so well preserved today?
a: It became a church early on
It lay underground for a long time
66963.e: Pope Boniface IV consecrated the building as a church in the year 609. Because it went on being used, it stayed in such good condition.
66963.m: The Pantheon has been a church since the year 609.

66964.q: Roughly how wide is the dome of the Pantheon?
66964.e: The dome measures about 43 metres. It is still the largest dome made of unreinforced concrete.
66964.m: The dome of the Pantheon is about 43 metres wide.

66965.q: Which famous Renaissance painter is buried in the Pantheon?
66965.e: Raphael died in Rome in 1520 and, as he had wished, was buried in the Pantheon. Later, Italian kings were buried there too.
66965.m: The painter Raphael is buried in the Pantheon.

66966.q: What building material is the dome of the Pantheon made of?
66966.e: The Romans mixed lime, volcanic ash and stones to make concrete. At the top they used lighter materials so the dome would weigh less.
66966.m: The dome of the Pantheon is cast in Roman concrete.

66967.q: Which goddess did the Vestal Virgins serve?
66967.e: Vesta was the Roman goddess of the hearth fire. Her priestesses were named Vestals after her.
66967.m: The Vestal Virgins served the goddess Vesta.

66968.q: What was the most important job of the Vestal Virgins?
66968.e: The sacred fire of Rome burned in the temple of Vesta. It must never go out, or people feared disaster for the city.
66968.m: The Vestal Virgins guarded the eternal fire of Rome.

66969.q: How many Vestal Virgins were there usually at the same time?
66969.e: Usually six Vestal Virgins served at the same time in the temple of Vesta.
66969.m: In Rome there were usually six Vestal Virgins.

66970.q: How many years did a Vestal Virgin’s service last?
66970.e: For ten years they learned, for ten years they served and for ten years they taught. After that they were allowed to leave.
66970.m: A Vestal Virgin served for 30 years.

66971.q: At what age were girls chosen as Vestal Virgins?
66971.e: The girls came from respected families. The chief priest, the Pontifex Maximus, chose them.
66971.m: Vestal Virgins were chosen as children.

66972.q: What standing did the Vestal Virgins have in Rome?
a: They were highly honoured and had special rights
They were poor servants without rights
They were seen as dangerous witches
66972.e: The Vestal Virgins were greatly respected. They had seats of honour at the games and could decide about their own property. Their leader was called the Virgo Vestalis Maxima.
66972.m: The Vestal Virgins were highly respected in Rome.

66973.q: What shape was the temple of Vesta in the Roman Forum?
66973.e: The round building was meant to recall old round huts. The sacred fire burned in its centre.
66973.m: The temple of Vesta in Rome was round.

66974.q: Where in Rome were the temple and house of the Vestal Virgins?
66974.e: The temple and the house of the Vestal Virgins, the Atrium Vestae, were in the Roman Forum. You can still visit their remains today.
66974.m: The Vestal Virgins lived in the Roman Forum.

66975.q: According to Norse belief, who went to the hall of Valhalla?
a: Warriors who had fallen in battle
66975.e: Valhalla was the hall of those who had fallen in battle. They were to live there until the end of the world.

66976.e: Odin was the chief god of Norse mythology. In Valhalla he gathered the best warriors around him.
66976.m: Odin was the lord of Valhalla.

66977.q: What were the female figures who brought fallen warriors to Valhalla called?
66977.e: The Valkyries chose the fallen on the battlefield. The word means something like “choosers of the slain”.
66977.m: The Valkyries led the fallen to Valhalla.

66978.q: What did the warriors in Valhalla do every day?
a: They practised fighting and feasted in the evening
66978.e: The warriors in Valhalla, the Einherjar, fought for practice during the day and feasted in the evening. In this way they prepared for the end of the world.
66978.m: In Valhalla the warriors practised fighting every day.

66979.q: According to the Edda, what was the roof of Valhalla covered with?
66979.e: The legend describes spear shafts as rafters and shields as roof tiles. This shows that Valhalla was a hall of warriors.
66979.m: The roof of Valhalla was covered with shields.

66980.q: What was special about the boar that was eaten in Valhalla every evening?
a: The next day it was alive again
66980.e: The boar Saehrimnir was cooked every evening. In the morning it was whole again, so the warriors always had enough to eat.
66980.m: The boar in Valhalla was whole again every day.

66981.q: What did the warriors in Valhalla drink?
66981.e: Mead is a drink made from honey. In the legend it flows from the udder of the goat Heidrun, who stands on the roof of Valhalla.
66981.m: In Valhalla the warriors drank mead.

66982.q: For which battle at the end of the world were the warriors in Valhalla preparing?
66982.e: At Ragnarök, gods and giants fight each other. The warriors from Valhalla are then meant to stand at Odin’s side.
66982.m: The warriors in Valhalla were waiting for Ragnarök.

66983.q: What were the priests of the Celts called?
66983.e: The druids were priests, judges and teachers. They passed on their knowledge by word of mouth.
66983.m: The priests of the Celts were called druids.

66984.q: How is the Celtic god Cernunnos usually shown?
66984.e: Cernunnos is seen as the lord of animals and nature. A well-known picture of him is on the Gundestrup cauldron.
66984.m: Cernunnos is the Celtic god with deer antlers.

66985.q: Which animals did the Celtic goddess Epona protect?
66985.e: Epona was the goddess of horses and riders. Roman cavalry soldiers also worshipped her.
66985.m: Epona was the Celtic goddess of horses.

66986.q: What was the Celtic god Taranis responsible for?
66986.e: Taranis was the god of thunder. He is often shown with a wheel, which probably stands for the sky or the sun.
66986.m: Taranis is the Celtic god of thunder.

66987.q: How do we know a lot about the gods of the Celts today?
a: From finds and from Roman reports
From many books by the druids
66987.e: The druids passed on their knowledge only by word of mouth. So what we know comes mainly from pictures, inscriptions and reports by Roman writers.
66987.m: We know a lot about Celtic gods from finds and Roman reports.

66988.q: Which site on Lake Neuchâtel gave its name to a period of Celtic culture?
66988.e: At La Tène many weapons and tools were found that were probably put into the water as offerings. That is why the later Iron Age is called the La Tène period.
66988.m: La Tène on Lake Neuchâtel gave its name to a Celtic period.

66989.q: Which region did the god Mithras originally come from?
66989.e: Mithras was originally a Persian god. The Romans took over his name and turned it into a secret cult.
66989.m: Mithras had his origins in Persia.

66990.q: What was the room where followers of Mithras met called?
66990.e: A mithraeum was usually a dark, cave-like room. Along the sides there were benches for the shared meal.
66990.m: Followers of Mithras met in a mithraeum.

66991.q: Which scene did the most important cult image of Mithras show?
66991.e: The killing of the bull is called the tauroctony. It could be seen in the centre of every mithraeum.
66991.m: The cult image shows Mithras killing the bull.

66992.q: Which group of people was particularly well represented in the cult of Mithras?
66992.e: Many mithraea were found near army camps on the edges of the Roman Empire. Traders and officials also belonged to it.
66992.m: Many followers of Mithras were Roman soldiers.

66993.q: Why do we know little today about the ceremonies of the cult of Mithras?
a: It only took place on ships
66993.e: Only initiated members could take part in the ceremonies, and they had to keep silent. They rose through seven grades of initiation.
66993.m: The cult of Mithras was a secret cult.

66994.q: What does the title “Pater”, held by the leader of a Mithras community, mean?
66994.e: Pater is Latin and means father. The Pater stood at the top of the seven grades of initiation.
66994.m: The highest grade in the cult of Mithras was the Pater.

66995.q: According to the myth, what was Mithras born from?
66995.e: Mithras is said to have come out of a rock. That is why he is also called the “rock-born”.
66995.m: According to the myth, Mithras was born from a rock.

66996.q: In which canton was a Roman sanctuary of Mithras dug up in Martigny?
66996.e: A mithraeum was discovered in Martigny in 1993. In Roman times Martigny was the main town of Valais.
66996.m: There is a Roman mithraeum in Martigny in Valais.

66997.q: Which city did King Gilgamesh rule?
66997.e: Gilgamesh was king of Uruk in the south of Mesopotamia. He is said to have built the great city wall.
66997.m: Gilgamesh was king of the city of Uruk.

66998.q: What was the name of Gilgamesh’s wild friend?
66998.e: The gods created Enkidu as a rival. After a fight, the two became close friends.

66999.q: In which script was the Epic of Gilgamesh written down?
66999.e: The epic was pressed into soft clay with a stylus. These wedge-shaped signs are called cuneiform.
66999.m: The Epic of Gilgamesh is written in cuneiform.

67000.q: What did Gilgamesh search for after his friend’s death?
67000.e: Enkidu’s death made Gilgamesh afraid of his own death. He travelled far to find eternal life.
67000.m: Gilgamesh searched in vain for eternal life.

67001.q: Which Bible story does the flood in the Epic of Gilgamesh remind you of?
67001.e: In the epic, a man survives the great flood in a ship with animals. This is very similar to the story of Noah.
67001.m: The flood story in the Epic of Gilgamesh is like Noah’s Ark.

67002.q: Which animal stole the plant of youth from Gilgamesh?
67002.e: While Gilgamesh was bathing, a snake ate the plant. Afterwards the snake shed its skin, but Gilgamesh was left with nothing.
67002.m: A snake stole the herb of youth from Gilgamesh.

67003.q: Which forest did the monster Humbaba guard?
67003.e: Gilgamesh and Enkidu went together into the Cedar Forest. There they defeated its guardian, Humbaba.
67003.m: Humbaba was the guardian of the Cedar Forest.

67004.q: What was the Epic of Gilgamesh found on?
67004.e: The tablets of baked clay come from an old library in Nineveh. They were dug up in the 19th century.
67004.m: The Epic of Gilgamesh is written on clay tablets.

67005.q: Which animal did the goddess Ishtar send against Gilgamesh?
67005.e: Ishtar was furious because Gilgamesh had rejected her. Gilgamesh and Enkidu killed the Bull of Heaven.
67005.m: Gilgamesh and Enkidu defeated the Bull of Heaven.

67006.q: What does the term animism mean?
a: Belief that nature has a soul
67006.e: In animism, people believe that animals, plants, mountains, rivers or stones have a soul or a spirit. This idea is found in many nature religions.
67006.m: In animism, animals, plants and things also have a soul.

67007.q: Which Latin word does “animism” come from?
67007.e: The Latin word “anima” means soul or breath. The name for the belief in things having a soul was made from it.
67007.m: The word animism comes from the Latin “anima”, meaning soul.

67008.q: What does a person with animist beliefs think about a large old tree?
a: The tree has a soul or a spirit
The tree belongs to the king
The tree was built by people
67008.e: In animism, trees, mountains and rivers also have a soul. That is why people treat them with respect.
67008.m: In animism, trees also have a soul.

67009.q: Which gate marks the entrance to a Shinto shrine in Japan?
67009.e: A torii is made of two posts and two crossbeams and is often painted red. It separates the everyday world from the holy area of the shrine.
67009.m: A torii is the gate to a Shinto shrine.

67010.q: Whose spirits are especially honoured in many animist religions?
67010.e: In many nature religions, ancestors who have died remain part of the family. People honour them and ask them for protection.
67010.m: Many nature religions honour the spirits of the ancestors.

a: A protective symbol of a group
67011.e: A totem is usually an animal or plant with which a family or clan feels closely connected. It is often seen as an ancestor or protector of the group.
67011.m: A totem is the protective symbol of a group.

67012.q: In Polynesia, what is the supernatural power that can work in people and things called?
67012.e: In Polynesia and Melanesia, mana is a mysterious power. Someone who has a lot of it is seen as powerful and respected.
67012.m: In Polynesia, the supernatural power is called mana.

67013.q: What do Aboriginal people in Australia call the time when the ancestral beings shaped the world?
67013.e: According to Aboriginal belief, in the Dreamtime ancestral beings created landscapes, animals and rules. This time is seen as still having an effect today.
67013.m: For Aboriginal people, the world was made in the Dreamtime.

67014.q: Which large red rock in Australia is a sacred place for the local Aboriginal people?
67014.e: Uluru belongs to the land of the Anangu. It is sacred to them, which is why climbing it has been banned since 2019.
67014.m: Uluru is a sacred rock of the Aboriginal people.

67015.q: Which region does the word “shaman” originally come from?
67015.e: The word comes from the language of the Evenks in Siberia. From there it passed through Russian into other languages.
67015.m: The word shaman comes from Siberia.

67016.q: Which instrument is especially important for Siberian shamans?
67016.e: With the steady beat of the drum, the shaman puts himself into a special state. The drum is often seen as his mount for riding into the spirit world.
67016.m: The drum is the most important tool of Siberian shamans.

67017.q: What state does a shaman enter during his ritual?
67017.e: According to the belief, in a trance the shaman is connected with the spirit world. Drumming, dancing and singing bring him into it.
67017.m: A shaman goes into a trance during his ritual.

67018.q: According to the belief of many Siberian peoples, what is a shaman’s task?
a: To act as a go-between for people and spirits
To write laws for the state
To look after the herds alone
67018.e: According to the belief, the shaman travels into the world of spirits. He is meant to heal the sick, ask for luck in hunting and bring back lost souls.
67018.m: The shaman is a go-between for people and spirits.

67019.q: In Siberian shamanism, into how many main worlds is the universe often divided?
67019.e: People often distinguish an upper, a middle and a lower world. The world tree connects these levels with each other.
67019.m: In Siberian shamanism there are often three worlds.

67020.q: On which lake in Siberia is the island of Olkhon a sacred place for shamans?
67020.e: On Olkhon stands Shaman Rock, an important place for the Buryats. Lake Baikal is the deepest lake on Earth.
67020.m: The island of Olkhon in Lake Baikal is a sacred place for shamans.

67021.q: What does the god Tengri, worshipped by Mongols and Turkic peoples, stand for?
67021.e: Tengri is the eternal blue sky. He was worshipped by Mongols and Turkic peoples and plays a role in Central Asian shamanism.
67021.m: Tengri is the sky god of the Mongols.

67022.q: What happened to the shamans in Siberia at the time of the Soviet Union?
67022.e: The Soviet government fought against religions. Many shamans were persecuted, and their drums were taken away or destroyed.
67022.m: In the Soviet Union, shamans were persecuted.

67023.q: Where do people still keep up shamanic customs today?
a: For example in Siberia and Mongolia
Nowhere in the world any more
Only in big cities in Europe
67023.e: After the end of the Soviet Union, shamanic customs came back to life in Siberia and Mongolia. There are shamans in many other parts of the world too.
67023.m: There are still shamans in Siberia and Mongolia today.

67024.e: Voodoo, also called vodun, comes from West Africa, especially from today’s Benin. The word comes from the language of the Fon.
67024.m: Voodoo originally comes from West Africa.

67025.q: In which West African country is 10 January a national holiday for voodoo?
67025.e: Since the 1990s, Benin has celebrated the “Fête du Vodoun” every year on 10 January. Many people in the country practise vodun.
67025.m: Benin celebrates Voodoo Day every year on 10 January.

67026.q: Which dark part of history is connected with the coast of Benin?
67026.e: In the past, many people were taken from port towns such as Ouidah to America as slaves. Today Ouidah is a centre of voodoo.
67026.m: In the past, many people from the coast of Benin were enslaved.

67027.q: Which animals are worshipped as sacred in a famous voodoo temple in Benin?
67027.e: Many royal pythons live in the Python Temple. The snakes are seen as sacred and must not be killed.
67027.m: In Benin there is a temple for sacred pythons.

67028.q: What does the word “vodun” roughly mean?
67028.e: In the language of the Fon in West Africa, vodun means something like spirit or deity.

67029.q: How did voodoo get from West Africa to Haiti?
67029.e: Enslaved people from West Africa brought their faith to the Caribbean. There it combined with parts of the Catholic faith.
67029.m: Enslaved people brought voodoo to Haiti.

67030.q: What are the spirit beings in Haitian voodoo called?
67030.e: The loa (also lwa) act as go-betweens for people and the highest god. Each loa has its own colours, songs and signs.
67030.m: In Haitian voodoo the spirits are called loa.

67031.q: Which vodun deity acts as guardian and opens the gate between people and spirits?
67031.e: Legba is called on first at ceremonies. According to the belief, other spirits cannot appear without his permission.
67031.m: In vodun, Legba opens the gate to the spirit world.

67032.q: What is true about the well-known voodoo dolls with pins?
a: They come mainly from films and novels
They are the most important ritual in Benin
They are worshipped in every temple
They are deities of the Fon
67032.e: The image of the voodoo doll was spread mainly by horror films and books. In the traditional vodun of West Africa, such dolls hardly play any role.
67032.m: Voodoo dolls are mainly an invention of films.

67033.e: The Yoruba worship many orishas. Each orisha is responsible for certain areas of life and nature.
67033.m: Orishas are the deities of the Yoruba.

67034.q: In which present-day country do most Yoruba live?
67034.e: The Yoruba live mainly in south-western Nigeria. There are also smaller groups in Benin and Togo.

67035.q: Why do the Yoruba usually turn to the orishas instead of their highest god?
a: The highest god is seen as far away
The highest god only speaks to kings
The highest god sleeps all year
67035.e: Olodumare, also called Olorun, is the highest creator god. He is far away, so people usually turn to the orishas.
67035.m: The highest god of the Yoruba is seen as far away.

67304.q: In which empire was the Blue Mosque built?
67304.e: The mosque was built from 1609 to 1616 under Sultan Ahmed I. Istanbul was then the capital of the Ottoman Empire.
67304.m: The Blue Mosque is an Ottoman building.

67305.q: Whose pupil was the architect of the Blue Mosque?
67305.e: The architect Mehmed Ağa had learned from the great Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan. He took on many of his teacher's ideas.
67305.m: The architect of the Blue Mosque was a pupil of Mimar Sinan.

67306.q: Why is it bright inside the Blue Mosque during the day?
a: Light comes in through many windows
The roof is made of glass
67306.e: Daylight comes into the prayer hall through about 260 windows. Today's coloured glass windows are copies of the old ones.
67306.m: Many windows make the Blue Mosque bright inside.

67307.q: What supports the large main dome of the Blue Mosque?
67307.e: The main dome is about 43 metres high. Several half-domes around it carry and support it.
67307.m: Half-domes support the main dome of the Blue Mosque.

67308.q: Where is Sultan Ahmed I buried?
a: In a tomb building next to the Blue Mosque
In the Taj Mahal in Agra
67308.e: Sultan Ahmed I rests in a türbe, a tomb building right next to his mosque. Members of his family, including later sultans, also lie there.
67308.m: Sultan Ahmed I is buried in a tomb building next to his mosque.

67309.q: What was a pope's visit to the Blue Mosque in 2006 meant to show?
a: That Christians and Muslims want to talk to each other
That the mosque would become a church
That the pope would become a Muslim
That the mosque would be closed
67309.e: Pope Benedict XVI visited the mosque in November 2006. It was a sign of dialogue between the religions.
67309.m: A papal visit in 2006 was a sign of dialogue between religions.

67310.q: Roughly how many handmade tiles decorate the inside of the Blue Mosque?
67310.e: More than 20,000 ceramic tiles with flowers and patterns were used inside. They gave the mosque its well-known nickname.
67310.m: More than 20,000 tiles decorate the Blue Mosque.

67311.q: What is the Blue Mosque today?
a: A mosque where people still pray
Only a museum with no prayers
67311.e: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque is still used for prayers today. Tourists may visit it outside prayer times.
67311.m: Muslims still pray in the Blue Mosque today.

67312.q: Who had the magnificent palaces of the Alhambra built?
67312.e: The Nasrids ruled the Emirate of Granada from the 13th century until 1492. The magnificent palaces were built during this time.
67312.m: Muslim rulers built the palaces of the Alhambra.

67313.q: In which Spanish city is the Alhambra?
67313.e: The Alhambra stands on a hill above Granada in Andalusia. Until 1492 it was the seat of the Muslim rulers.

67315.q: Which ruler had a Renaissance-style palace built in the Alhambra?
67315.e: Charles V ordered the palace in 1527. It was never fully finished and today houses museums.
67315.m: In the middle of the Alhambra stands a Renaissance palace of Charles V.

67316.q: Which country did the writer Washington Irving come from, who made the Alhambra famous with his stories?
67316.e: The American Washington Irving lived in the Alhambra for a few months in 1829. His “Tales of the Alhambra” attracted many travellers to Granada.
67316.m: Washington Irving made the Alhambra famous with his stories.

67317.q: What was the Alcazaba, the oldest part of the Alhambra, used for?
67317.e: The Alcazaba is the military part with towers and walls. From there soldiers kept watch over the city.
67317.m: The Alcazaba is the fortress of the Alhambra.

67318.q: Which Dutch artist was inspired by the tile patterns of the Alhambra?
67318.e: M. C. Escher copied the tile patterns in the Alhambra. After that he created his famous pictures of figures that fit together without gaps.
67318.m: The patterns of the Alhambra inspired the artist M. C. Escher.

67319.q: What was the name of the woman for whom the Taj Mahal was built as a tomb?
67319.e: Shah Jahan had the Taj Mahal built for his favourite wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in 1631. Her name means something like “the chosen one of the palace”.
67319.m: The Taj Mahal is the tomb of Mumtaz Mahal.

67320.q: In which century was the Taj Mahal built?
67320.e: Building began in 1632, shortly after the death of Mumtaz Mahal. The whole site was only finished after many years.
67320.m: The Taj Mahal was built in the 17th century.

67321.q: Roughly how many craftsmen worked on the Taj Mahal?
67321.e: More than 20,000 craftsmen from India and other countries worked on the Taj Mahal. About 1,000 elephants helped to transport the building materials.
67321.m: Over 20,000 craftsmen built the Taj Mahal.

67322.q: Why do the four minarets of the Taj Mahal lean slightly outwards?
a: So that they would not fall onto the tomb in an earthquake
Because the ground was too soft
67322.e: The minarets lean slightly on purpose. If they collapsed, they would fall away from the main building.
67322.m: The minarets of the Taj Mahal lean outwards to protect the tomb.

67323.q: What are the coloured flower patterns in the white marble of the Taj Mahal made with?
67323.e: Craftsmen cut semi-precious stones precisely and set them into the marble. This created flowers and bands of writing that never fade.
67323.m: The patterns on the Taj Mahal are made of inlaid semi-precious stones.

a: In the Taj Mahal next to his wife
67324.e: Shah Jahan's sarcophagus stands next to his wife's. Because it was added later, it is the only element that is not placed symmetrically.
67324.m: Shah Jahan rests in the Taj Mahal next to Mumtaz Mahal.

67325.q: How is the garden in front of the Taj Mahal laid out?
a: In four equal parts with water channels
As a rock garden without plants
67325.e: The garden is a charbagh, a Persian garden in four parts. In the middle there is a long pool in which the tomb is reflected.
67325.m: The garden of the Taj Mahal is divided into four parts.

67326.q: Which famous list is the Taj Mahal on because it is valuable for all of humanity?
67326.e: UNESCO has added the Taj Mahal to the World Heritage List. Such places are to be preserved for all people.
67326.m: The Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

67327.q: Why is the Arabic script Naskh the one most often used for books today?
a: Because it is easy to read
Because it is the oldest script
Because it runs from left to right
67327.e: Naskh is clear and easy to read. That is why it is used most for books and the printed Quran.
67327.m: Naskh is the most common Arabic book script.

67328.q: Where do you often see Arabic calligraphy as large, sweeping bands of writing?
a: On the walls and domes of mosques
67328.e: Grand scripts such as Thuluth decorate the walls and domes of many mosques. They often show verses from the Quran.
67328.m: Mosques are often decorated with large bands of writing.

67329.q: Which language apart from Arabic is also written with Arabic letters?
67329.e: Persian is written with Arabic letters. The elegant, hanging script style Nastaliq also developed in Persia.
67329.m: Persian is also written with Arabic letters.

67330.q: Why did the Ottomans write their official documents in a very dense, ornate script?
a: So that they were beautiful and hard to forge
So that they could be read faster
Because children were meant to write them
67330.e: The Diwani script developed in the Ottoman chancery, the Divan. The dense script was beautiful and hard to forge.
67330.m: The Ottomans wrote their official documents in the Diwani script.

67331.q: Why is the Prophet Muhammad often described in Islamic art with words instead of a picture?
a: Because many Muslims do not show him in pictures
Because there were no colours at the time
67331.e: Many Muslims do not show Muhammad in pictures. A panel of writing, the hilye, therefore describes his appearance and character in words.
67331.m: A hilye describes Muhammad with artistic writing instead of a picture.

67332.q: North-west Africa is called the Maghreb in Arabic. What does this word mean?
67332.e: Maghreb means “west”, the land where the sun sets. The Maghribi script style also comes from there.

67334.q: What is typical of the everyday Arabic script Ruq'a?
a: It can be written quickly by hand
It is only used for the Quran
It runs from left to right
67334.e: Ruq'a has short, simple shapes and can be written quickly. Many people in Arab countries use it for handwriting.
67334.m: Ruq'a is a fast everyday script.

67335.q: In which direction is Arabic script written?
67335.e: Arabic is written from right to left. That is why, from our point of view, an Arabic book begins “at the back”.
67335.m: Arabic is written from right to left.

67336.q: The word “arabesque” originally comes from which language?
67336.e: The word comes from the Italian “arabesco”, which means “Arabic”. Europeans used it for the decoration they knew from Islamic art.

67337.q: What is special about the pattern of an arabesque?
67337.e: An arabesque has no fixed beginning and no end. Many see this as a sign of God's infinity.
67337.m: An arabesque can be continued without end.

67338.q: For which instrument did Robert Schumann write his piece “Arabeske” in 1839?
67338.e: Robert Schumann composed the “Arabeske”, Op. 18, for piano. Like the ornament, the music is playful and intertwined.
67338.m: Robert Schumann wrote a piano piece called “Arabeske”.

67339.q: Claude Debussy wrote the well-known “Deux Arabesques”. What was Debussy's job?
67339.e: Claude Debussy was a French composer. His two arabesques for piano are among his best-known pieces.
67339.m: Claude Debussy composed two arabesques for piano.

67340.q: What is an arabesque in ballet?
a: A pose on one leg with the other leg stretched out behind
67340.e: In an arabesque the dancer stands on one leg and stretches the other far out behind. The long line recalls the sweeping ornament.
67340.m: In ballet, the arabesque is a pose on one leg.

67341.q: What are the colourful zellige patterns in Morocco made of?
67341.e: Zellige are mosaics made of hand-cut clay tiles. In Morocco they decorate fountains, walls and floors.

67342.e: Arabesques are mainly made of curving plant shapes. Tendrils, leaves and flowers seem to grow into each other endlessly.
67342.m: Arabesques are made of plant shapes.

67343.q: What shapes are many geometric patterns in Islamic art made of?
67343.e: Such patterns are called girih, which means “knot” in Persian. Crossing lines form stars and polygons.
67343.m: Girih patterns are made of stars and polygons.

67344.q: What does the abbreviation “AH” after an Islamic year mean?
a: In the year of the Hijra
67344.e: The Islamic calendar counts the years from Muhammad's emigration to Medina. That is why you write, for example, “1448 AH”.
67344.m: The abbreviation “AH” means “in the year of the Hijra”.

67345.q: What do many Muslims celebrate in the month of Rabi al-Awwal?
67345.e: The festival is called Mawlid an-Nabi and for many Sunnis falls on 12 Rabi al-Awwal. Shias often celebrate it a few days later.
67345.m: In the month of Rabi al-Awwal many Muslims celebrate Muhammad's birthday.

67346.q: In which month of our calendar did the Islamic year 1448 begin?
67346.e: The Islamic New Year 1448 fell in mid-June 2026. Because the lunar year is shorter, the year 1449 begins about eleven days earlier, still in June 2027.
67346.m: The Islamic year 1448 began in June 2026.

67347.q: Traditionally, how do you recognise the beginning of a new Islamic month?
a: By the first thin crescent moon
67347.e: The month begins when the first crescent moon, the hilal, can be seen after the new moon. Today some countries also calculate the start in advance.
67347.m: An Islamic month begins with the first crescent moon.

67348.q: On which day of the month of Muharram is the day of remembrance Ashura?
67348.e: Ashura comes from the Arabic word for ten. On this day Shias especially remember the death of Husayn at Karbala.
67348.m: Ashura is on the tenth day of Muharram.

67349.q: A lunar month lasts about 29.5 days. How many days do 12 such months have together?
67349.e: 12 times 29.5 days makes 354 days. That is about 11 days fewer than a solar year of 365 days.
67349.m: Twelve lunar months last about 354 days together.

67350.q: Which country officially uses an Islamic solar calendar whose year begins at the start of spring?
67350.e: Iran also counts the years from the Hijra, but by the sun. New Year is the Nowruz festival at the beginning of spring.
67350.m: Iran has an Islamic solar calendar with New Year in spring.

67351.q: How many days can a month in the Islamic calendar have?
67351.e: About 29.5 days pass from one crescent moon to the next. That is why a month has either 29 or 30 days.
67351.m: An Islamic month has 29 or 30 days.

67352.q: Which animal is basically forbidden by Islamic food rules?
67352.e: The Quran clearly forbids pork. Meat from cattle, sheep and goats is allowed if it has been slaughtered correctly.

67353.q: Why do many Muslims check the ingredients of jelly sweets?
a: Because gelatine often comes from pigs
67353.e: Gelatine is often made from pig skin. But there are also jelly sweets made with beef gelatine or plant ingredients.
67353.m: Gelatine in sweets often comes from pigs.

67354.q: What does a halal certificate confirm?
a: That a product is allowed by Islamic rules
That a product comes from Switzerland
That a product is especially cheap
67354.e: An inspection body checks the ingredients and how the product is made. If it meets the rules, it may carry a halal mark.
67354.m: A halal certificate confirms that a product is allowed.

67355.q: What has been banned in Switzerland since a popular vote in 1893?
67355.e: In 1893 the people approved the first federal popular initiative, the ban on ritual slaughter. Today the Animal Welfare Act says that mammals must be stunned before slaughter.
67355.m: In Switzerland mammals must be stunned before slaughter.

67356.q: So where do Muslims in Switzerland often get ritually slaughtered meat from?
67356.e: Importing meat from religious slaughter is allowed. This is how Muslims and Jews in Switzerland get meat according to their rules.
67356.m: Ritually slaughtered meat may be imported into Switzerland.

67357.q: In which Asian country does a state authority issue a halal mark that is known worldwide?
67357.e: In Malaysia the state authority JAKIM issues the halal mark. Its certificate is recognised in many countries.
67357.m: In Malaysia a state authority checks whether products are halal.

67358.q: What do many Muslims do if it is unclear whether a food is halal?
a: They prefer to go without it.
They only eat it on Fridays.
They simply cook it for longer.
67358.e: Doubtful foods are called mashbooh. Many Muslims avoid them until it is clear what they are made of.
67358.m: With doubtful foods, many Muslims prefer to go without.

67359.q: Apart from food, which products can also have halal certificates?
67359.e: Creams, lipsticks or capsules can also contain substances from pigs or alcohol. That is why some companies have them certified.
67359.m: Cosmetics and medicines can also be certified halal.

67360.q: What is forbidden in Islamic banking?
67360.e: The Quran forbids riba, which is usually understood as interest. Islamic banks therefore earn their money in other ways.
67360.m: Islamic banks do not charge interest.

67361.q: What is the Arabic word for the forbidden interest?
67361.e: Riba literally means “increase”. It refers to a fixed, agreed profit from money that is lent.
67361.m: The forbidden interest is called riba.

a: The bank buys goods and sells them on at a mark-up
The bank charges interest every month
67362.e: For example, the bank buys a car and sells it to the customer at a higher, fixed price. The customer pays it off in instalments, without interest.
67362.m: With murabaha the bank earns from a price mark-up.

67363.q: Where does the return on Islamic bonds, called sukuk, come from?
a: From rents or profits of a real asset
67363.e: Anyone who buys sukuk gets a share in an asset such as a building. The return comes from rents or profits instead of interest.
67363.m: Sukuk are Islamic bonds without interest.

67364.q: How does the Islamic insurance takaful work?
a: Members pay into a shared pot and help each other
Everyone only pays when they are ill
67364.e: With takaful, members pay into a shared pot. From it they help each other when damage or loss happens.
67364.m: Takaful is insurance according to Islamic rules.

67365.q: Which businesses are Islamic banks not allowed to invest in?
67365.e: Businesses involving alcohol, pork or gambling are considered haram. A board of scholars checks the bank's investments.
67365.m: Islamic banks do not invest in gambling and alcohol.

67366.q: What does mudaraba mean in Islamic banking?
a: One person gives money, the other does the work, and they share the profit
67366.e: In mudaraba, one person provides the capital and the other their knowledge and work. Profits are shared according to an agreed ratio.
67366.m: In mudaraba, the investor and the entrepreneur share the profit.

67367.q: In which country does the Islamic Development Bank have its headquarters?
67367.e: The Islamic Development Bank began its work in 1975. It is based in Jeddah in Saudi Arabia and supports projects in Muslim countries.
67367.m: The Islamic Development Bank is based in Saudi Arabia.

67368.q: What can you find in the courtyard of many mosques?
67368.e: Many mosques have a courtyard with a fountain in front of the prayer hall. There worshippers wash before prayer.
67368.m: In the courtyard of many mosques there is a fountain for washing.

67369.q: What are many mosques in Iran especially known for?
a: Colourful tiles in blue and turquoise
67369.e: Many Iranian mosques are decorated with bright tiles. They often have large arched halls open to the courtyard, called iwans.
67369.m: Iranian mosques are known for their colourful tiles.

67370.q: In which country is the Great Mosque of Djenné, the largest mud building in the world?
67370.e: The mosque in Djenné is built of mud bricks. Every year the inhabitants repair the layer of mud together at a festival.
67370.m: The mud mosque of Djenné is in Mali.

67371.q: What shape is the famous minaret of the Great Mosque of Samarra in Iraq?
67371.e: The Malwiya minaret is a spiral with a ramp winding up around it. It was built in the 9th century.
67371.m: The minaret of Samarra winds upwards like a spiral.

67372.e: In the 16th century Mimar Sinan built many magnificent mosques for the sultans. His masterpiece is the Selimiye Mosque in Edirne.
67372.m: Mimar Sinan was the greatest architect of the Ottomans.

67373.q: In which mosque is one of the largest hand-knotted carpets in the world?
a: Sheikh Zayed Mosque in Abu Dhabi
Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem
67373.e: The huge carpet of the Sheikh Zayed Mosque was made in Iran by more than 1,000 carpet weavers. It covers the whole prayer hall.
67373.m: One of the largest carpets in the world is in Abu Dhabi.

67374.q: What is the fountain in the courtyard of many Turkish mosques for?
a: As a wishing well for coins
67374.e: In Turkish the fountain is called a şadırvan and has many taps all around it. Worshippers wash there before prayer.
67374.m: Worshippers wash at the mosque fountain before prayer.

67375.q: On which day of the week do Muslims meet for the important communal prayer in the mosque?
67375.e: Friday midday prayer is the most important communal prayer of the week. Large mosques for it are called Friday mosques.
67375.m: The communal Friday prayer takes place in a Friday mosque.

67376.q: Why is the Quran often placed on a small stand for reading?
a: So that it does not touch the floor
So that nobody can read it
So that it is not stolen
67376.e: The Quran is treated with great respect. That is why, when it is read, it lies on a wooden stand called a kursi.
67376.m: The Quran lies on a kursi when it is read.

67377.q: Which mosque in Jerusalem is considered the third holiest site in Islam?
67377.e: After Mecca and Medina, the Al-Aqsa Mosque is the holiest place for many Muslims. It stands on the Temple Mount near the Dome of the Rock.
67377.m: The Al-Aqsa Mosque is the third holiest site in Islam.

67378.q: In which city in Iraq is the shrine of Imam Husayn?
67378.e: Husayn, a grandson of Muhammad, died in 680 at the Battle of Karbala. His tomb is one of the most important places of pilgrimage for Shias.
67378.m: The tomb of Imam Husayn is in Karbala.

67379.q: Whose tomb do pilgrims visit in the Iraqi city of Najaf?
67379.e: The golden shrine of Ali ibn Abi Talib stands in Najaf. Ali was Muhammad's son-in-law and, for Shias, the first imam.
67379.m: The tomb of Ali is in Najaf.

67380.q: In which country is the pilgrimage city of Mashhad with the shrine of Imam Reza?
67380.e: Mashhad is home to the shrine of Imam Reza, the eighth imam of the Shias. Millions of pilgrims come every year.
67380.m: The shrine of Imam Reza is in Mashhad in Iran.

67381.q: Whose tomb in Konya do many people visit?
67381.e: The mystic and poet Jalal ad-Din Rumi died in Konya in 1273. His tomb in the Mevlana Museum is a popular place of pilgrimage.
67381.m: The poet Rumi is buried in Konya.

67382.q: On which continent is the pilgrimage city of Touba with the great festival Grand Magal?
67382.e: Touba is in Senegal in West Africa. Every year hundreds of thousands of people, often more than a million, come to the Grand Magal.
67382.m: The pilgrimage city of Touba is in Senegal in Africa.

67383.q: When was the Great Mosque of Kairouan in Tunisia founded?
67383.e: The Great Mosque of Kairouan is one of the oldest mosques in North Africa. Many Muslims see the city as a holy place.
67383.m: Kairouan is a holy city in Tunisia.

67384.q: Who is buried in the Eyüp Sultan Mosque in Istanbul?
67384.e: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari was a companion of Muhammad and died near Constantinople. Atatürk is buried in Ankara and Rumi in Konya.
67384.m: A companion of Muhammad is buried in the Eyüp Sultan Mosque.

67385.q: Who visits the Sufi shrine of Moinuddin Chishti in India?
67385.e: The tomb of the Sufi master Moinuddin Chishti in Ajmer attracts people of many religions. He lived in the 12th and 13th centuries.
67385.m: The shrine of Moinuddin Chishti attracts people of many religions.

67386.q: In Egypt, how are people traditionally woken during Ramadan for the meal before dawn?
a: A man walks through the streets with a drum
67386.e: The drummer is called the mesaharati. At night he beats his drum and calls out names so that nobody misses suhoor.
67386.m: In Egypt the mesaharati wakes people for suhoor.

67387.q: What do people in Turkey hang between the minarets of large mosques during Ramadan?
a: Messages made of little lights, called mahya
67387.e: Mahya are messages made of lights strung between two minarets. The tradition goes back to Ottoman times.
67387.m: In Turkey, mahya light up between the minarets during Ramadan.

67388.q: What do millions of people in Indonesia do at the end of Ramadan?
a: They travel to their families in the villages
They go on a skiing holiday
They go on a pilgrimage to Rome
67388.e: This great journey home is called mudik. Roads, ferries and trains are then completely full.
67388.m: Mudik is the great journey home in Indonesia at the end of Ramadan.

67389.q: What do families in Indonesia and Malaysia like to eat at the festival at the end of Ramadan?
a: Ketupat, rice in woven palm leaves
67389.e: Ketupat is rice cooked in small baskets made of palm leaves. It is as much a part of the festival as being together with family.
67389.m: Ketupat is a festive dish in Indonesia and Malaysia.

67390.q: What do children in Qatar do at the Garangao festival in the middle of Ramadan?
a: They collect sweets from house to house
67390.e: At Garangao, children in traditional clothes go from house to house. They sing songs and are given sweets and nuts.
67390.m: At Garangao, children in Qatar collect sweets.

67391.q: In Sarajevo, how is the breaking of the fast announced every evening during Ramadan?
a: With a cannon shot from a fortress
67391.e: At sunset a cannon is fired from the Yellow Bastion above the city. Then iftar begins in Sarajevo.
67391.m: In Sarajevo a cannon shot announces the breaking of the fast.

67392.q: Why do fasting days in summer last longer in Switzerland than in Mecca?
a: Because the days are longer in the north in summer
